newsitem.title: USA: Kennametal sees lower Q3 on German softness.
newsitem.headline: Kennametal sees lower Q3 on German softness.

text.p: Kennametal Inc said Monday it expects sales for the third quarter ending March 31 to be in the range of $290 million to $295 million and earnings to be in the range of $0.70 to $0.75 per share.

Kennametal had fiscal 1996 third quarter earnings of $0.88 per share on sales of $286.1 million. The projected earnings are well below the $0.92 per share First Call consensus estimate for the current quarter.
Kennametal said the expected decline in earnings is primarily a result of continued weak sales in Germany and a 10 percent decline in the mark.
Sales in Germany are expected to be down 20 percent or $10 million from the prior year quarter, including the impact of foreign currency translation effects, the company said.

Additionally, Kennametal said, operating expenses could increase during the quarter as a result of continued investments in the industrial supply market to further augment the company's geographic expansion plans, coupled with relocation expenses related to the new corporate headquarters.

Chief Financial Officer Richard J. Orwig said, "We had originally anticipated that conditions in Germany would be flat with last year or even start to show improvement in early 1997; however, this did not occur.

"We believe that we are well positioned to benefit from any improvement in economic conditions in Germany. Our other markets continue to perform and we expect to report an increase in sales in the industrial supply market of over 25 percent."
